 Order

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This petition under Section 439 (2) of Cr.P.C. has been filed for cancellation of bail granted to respondent No. 2 vide order dated 24.1.2024 by Additional Sessions Judge, Chachoda in Bail Application No. 13/2024 related to Crime No.04/2024 registered at Police Station - Mrigwas,
District - Guna.

2. As per prosecution story, on 09.1.2024, prosecutrix lodged a complaint at the police station to the effect that on 05.12.2023, when she was alone in her house, respondent No. 2 / accused entered into the house and committed rape upon her.

Upon this, FIR bearing Crime No. 04/2024 was registered against respondent No. 2 / accused for offence under Sections 376, 457 and 506 of IPC and during the course of investigation, respondent No. 2 was arrested.

Respondent No. 2 filed bail application before the court below NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22114 2 MCRC-14839-2024 which was allowed vide order impugned for cancellation of which present petition has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that respondent No. 2 has been granted benefit of bail without considering the gravity of offence and material available on record.
Learned Court below in a casual manner granted bail to respondent No. 2 only on the ground of delay in FIR.

It is further argued that respondent No. 2 / accused is also giving threat to the prosecutrix to change her Prosecutrix Through Crime No.04/2024 vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79930995/
1 statement in the Court.

entities.text: No.04/2024 vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, prayed to recall / cancel the bail granted to respondent No. 2.
However, learned counsel for the petitioner conceded that there there is no violation of any condition of bail order.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No. 2 vehemently opposed the petition and argued that learned court below after considering all aspects of the case granted bail to respondent No. 2.
There is no ground i.e. breach of any condition of bail order, therefore, the petition is liable to be dismissed.

5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.
6.

The Supreme Court in the case of Himanshu Sharma vs. State of Madhya Pradesh; Criminal Appeals arising out of SlP (Criminal) No(s). 786 of 2024 and 2032 of 2024, decided on 20.2.2024,
laid down circumstances for cancellation of bail which are mentioned below:-
"Generally the grounds for cancellation of bail, broadly, are, (i) the accused misuses his liberty by indulging in similar criminal activity, (ii) interferes NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22114 3 MCRC-14839-2024 with the course of investigation, (iii) attempts to tamper with evidence or witnesses, (iv) threatens witnesses or indulges in similar activities which would hamper smooth investigation,
(v) there is likelihood of his fleeing to another country, (vi) attempts to make himself scarce by going underground or becoming unavailable to the investigating agency,

entities.text: Himanshu Sharma vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (vii) attempts to place himself beyond the reach of his surety, etc.

These grounds are illustrative and not exhaustive."
7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in case the case of Dolat Ram Vs. State of Haryana [(1995) 1 SCC 349 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 237]

entities.text: Dolat Ram Vs. State of Haryana [(1995) 1 SCC 349 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 237]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
has held as under:
"Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the cancellation of the bail, already granted.

Generally speaking, the grounds for cancellation of bail, broadly (illustrative and not exhaustive) are: interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of Justice or evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner.
The satisfaction of the court, on the basis of material placed on the record of the possibility of the accused absconding is yet another reason justifying the cancellation of bail.

However, bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial.

These principles, it appears, were lost sight of by the High Court when it decided to cancel the bail,
already granted.

The High Court it appears to us overlooked the distinction of the factors relevant for rejecting bail in a non-bailable case in the first instance and the cancellation of bail already granted"
Prosecutrix Through Crime No.04/2024 vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79930995/
2

entities.text: Prosecutrix Through Crime No.04/2024 vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22114 4 MCRC-14839-2024 8.
In this case, the record reflects that learned Court below while deciding the bail considered all the material aspects and granted bail.
The counsel for the petitioner himself conceded that this is not a case of breach of condition of bail order.
Thus, it is apparent that respondent No. 2 has not misused the liberty of bail granted to him.

9. So far as the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner that respondent No. 2 is giving threat to the prosecutrix is concerned, there is nothing on record to show that any complaint before the Police or before the Court below has been filed by the prosecutrix in this regard.
10. It is trite law that while exercising the jurisdiction under Section 439 (2) of CrPC, this Court cannot act as an appellate Court.

Under these circumstances, in view of the settled principle of law,
as discussed above, this is not a fit case for cancellation of bail.
11. Accordingly, present petition is dismissed having no merits.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS Prosecutrix Through Crime No.04/2024 vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79930995/
